Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.text: Who shall not fear thee, O Lord? For all nations shall come and worship before thee, for thy judgments are made manifest.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments made manifest are his prophecies and his laws coming to pass before everyone's eyes.

This is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” When all nations come and worship before the Most High, they are no longer fierce against Israel. They are subdued. That is what the Lord is saying here: these nations will be brought down and made to come and worship before him.

So the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, the nations whose languages we cannot understand, will not be seen raging against us any more. They will be bowing before the King, because the Lord only is holy and all the nations will fear him.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened”: everything the prophets wrote, the testimony, is opened, meaning we are understanding it and teaching it. Then “the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues”, and received “seven golden vials full of the wrath of God”, and a great voice said, “Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.” The testimonies speak of the judgment and death that has to take place on the earth.

But before that can happen, something has to happen first. Amos reads: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” That is the lion we read in Ezra, roaring and chasing the eagle out of the wood. “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” The trumpet is the witnesses, us teaching; when we testify, the people better be afraid. “Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The Lord is behind it, through the angels with the seven last plagues.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The prophets are his witnesses, and the secret he reveals to them is his testimonies. And when he reveals it to us, we are supposed to testify.

“The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” The lion roaring is Christ speaking to us, and we prophesy. “Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”: Ashdod is modern-day Tel Aviv in the land of Israel, and the land of Egypt is America. That is where we have to testify, and then the plagues are poured out.

moments.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

points: Remember what the Lord said: I will smite Egypt with plagues as before. Them seven plagues are the plagues the Lord is bringing on America.
The seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues, and one of the four beasts gave unto them seven golden vials full of the wrath of God. Them seven plagues are the wrath of God.
